mission_06: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus connects differentiation and integration. Part 1: if F(x) = integral from a to x of f(t)dt, then F'(x) = f(x). Part 2: the definite integral from a to b equals F(b) - F(a) where F is any antiderivative. This theorem shows that integration and differentiation are inverse operations. The accumulation function G(x) builds up area as x increases, and its rate of change at any point equals the function value. This deep connection is used everywhere in physics (work = integral of force), probability (CDF is integral of PDF), and ML (computing cumulative distributions).
